items.content_excerpt: $ONDS At What Price Do Short Sellers Start to Panic? *Level 1: $6.00 – A Little Sweaty* If the stock crosses *$6*, short sellers start to take notice—but there’s no panic yet. *Level 2: $7.07 – PANIC SETS IN* 🔥 This is the *most critical point*—it’s the *60-day moving average* combined with *resistance*. If we break through *$7.07*, short sellers will be forced to trigger their *stop-losses*, which automatically turns into *buying*. In other words, a *self-sustaining* rally begins. *This* is the point where your *call options* take off. *Level 3: $8.43 – $8.76 – TOTAL CHAOS* 🚀 This marks the *200-day moving average*. If the price reaches this level, there won’t be any short sellers left; they’ll all shift into "buy at any cost" mode. If we see the price climb *above $8.50*, we can start talking about *$10*.

FINRA: SI fell from 36.4M (7/31) to 16.8M (8/31), so ~19.5M were covered on the OTC in one month (on news volume). Since mid-Sept the remaining ~16M has been flat, even on 7 days with >2.5M volume. items.title: $NLST short volume is not short interest aka someone short selling … That 47.86% (1.11M shares) is daily short volume, not actual shorting—a
items.content_excerpt: $NLST short volume is not short interest aka someone short selling … That 47.86% (1.11M shares) is daily short volume, not actual shorting—and it’s actually down from yesterday’s 52.87%. On the OTC, broker-dealers don’t warehouse inventory, so whenever a retail buy order comes in and they fill it before locating shares, FINRA logs it as a "short sale" even if they buy it back minutes later. Actual open short bets are tracked in bi-monthly Short Interest, while today’s 10M flat borrow pool and falling 1.81% borrow fee prove shorts weren't piling on. 👇🏼👇🏼👇🏼
